div.head: Leis Wl 38
div.ab: Dous sunt perceners de un’ erithet, e est l’un enplaidé senz l’altre, et per sa folie si pert, ne d[e]it pur ço l’altre estre perdant, qui present ne [f]ud; kar jose juge[e] entre eus ne forsjuge pas les altres, qui ne sunt a present.

Ne quis ex iudicio alterius preiudicium paciatur. Si duo aut plures hereditatem parciantur, et unus sine altero uel aliis in ius uocatus ex insipiencia uel alio casu amiserit, non debent partiarii inde dampnum sentire; quia res inter alios iudicata aliis non preiudicat, presertim si presentes non fuerunt.

Dous sunt perceners de un erithet, e est l'un enplaidé senz l'altre, et per sa folie si pert, ne d[e]it pur ço l'altre estre perdant qui present ne [f]ud, kar jose juge[e] entre eus ne forsjuge pas les altres qui ne sunt a present.

38. Zwei sind Theilhaber einer Erbschaft, und der eine wird ohne den andern verklagt und verliert durch seine Thorheit: nicht soll deshalb der andere, welcher nicht anwesend war, Verlierer sein; denn eine zwischen jenen entschiedene Sache präjudicirt nicht den andern, welche nicht gegenwärtig sind.

38. Two are partners in an inheritance, and the one is accused without the other and loses through his folly: the other, who was not present, shall not on that account be a loser; for a matter decided between those does not prejudice the others, who are not present.

If two men are sharers in an inheritance, and one is charged without the other, and loses [the case] through his folly, the other who was not present shall not be a loser because of that, for a judgment given in a case between those concerned cannot affect injuriously others who are not present.

Justinians Codex c. 14 C. 3, 36 und c. 8 C. 8, 45, die Schmid vergleicht, passen nicht genau. Das Zitat bei Conrat (Gesch. Röm. Rechts im MA. I 628) scheint mir richtig, das Zusammentreffen nicht (wie ihm) möglicherweise zufällig: Res inter alios iudicatae neque emolumentum afferre his qui iudicio non interfuerunt neque praeiudicium solent irrogare. Ideoque nepti tuae praeiudicare non potest quod aduersus coheredes eius iudicatum est; 7, 56, 4: nec in simili negotio res inter alios acta praeiudicare

Justinian’s Codex c. 14 C. 3, 36 and c. 8 C. 8, 45, which Schmid compares, do not fit exactly. The citation in Conrat (Gesch. Röm. Rechts im MA. I 628) seems to me correct, and the coincidence not (as it does to him) possibly accidental: Res inter alios iudicatae neque emolumentum afferre his qui iudicio non interfuerunt neque praeiudicium solent irrogare.
